sanskrit: sa tu tasya mahānādaṃ śrutvā vaivasvato yamaḥ śatruṃ vijayinaṃ mene svabalasya ca saṃkṣayam
english: Hearing that great roar, Yama Vaivasvata reckoned his enemy to be victorious and perceived the decimation of his own army.

sanskrit: sa tu yodhān hatān matvā krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ abravīt tvaritaṃ sūtaṃ rathaḥ samupanīyatām
english: Seeing his warriors slain, his eyes blazing with fury, he quickly commanded his charioteer: "Bring up the chariot at once."

sanskrit: tasya sūto rathaṃ divyam upasthāpya mahāsvanam sthitaḥ sa ca mahātejā āruroha mahāratham
english: His charioteer drew up the divine chariot, whose thunder was tremendous; and that one of great splendour mounted the great car.

sanskrit: pāśamudgarahastaś ca mṛtyus tasyāgrato sthitaḥ yena saṃkṣipyate sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram
english: Death, noose and club in hand — by whom all three worlds, moving and unmoving, are brought to their end — stood before him.

sanskrit: kāladaṇḍaś ca pārśvastho mūrtimān syandane sthitaḥ yamapraharaṇaṃ divyaṃ prajvalann iva tejasā
english: The staff of Time, embodied and blazing as though with divine lustre — Yama's celestial weapon — stood at his side upon the chariot.

sanskrit: tato lokās trayas trastāḥ kampante ca divaukasaḥ kālaṃ kruddhaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā lokatrayabhayāvaham
english: Then the three worlds trembled in terror and the dwellers in heaven shook, beholding Time in wrath, dread to all the three worlds.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu te taṃ vikṛtaṃ rathaṃ mṛtyusamanvitam sacivā rākṣasendrasya sarvalokabhayāvaham
english: The ministers of the lord of rākṣasas, beholding that terrible chariot attended by Death, terrifying to every world—

sanskrit: laghusattvatayā sarve naṣṭasaṃjñā bhayārditāḥ nātra yoddhuṃ samarthāḥ sma ity uktvā vipradudruvuḥ
english: —all, their senses lost in the lightness of their nature, overcome with fear, cried out "We cannot fight here!" and fled in all directions.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathaṃ lokabhayāvaham nākṣubhyata tadā rakṣo vyathā caivāsya nābhavat
english: But the rākṣasa, seeing that chariot so terrifying to the worlds, was not agitated; no distress arose in him at all.

sanskrit: sa tu rāvaṇam āsādya visṛjañ śaktitomarān yamo marmāṇi saṃkruddho rākṣasasya nyakṛntata
english: Yama, closing on Rāvaṇa and hurling javelins and iron clubs, struck with great fury at the vital points of the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu sthitaḥ svasthaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mumoca ha tasmin vaivasvatarathe toyavarṣam ivāmbudaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, standing composed, poured a shower of arrows onto Vaivasvata's chariot as a cloud pours a rain of water.

sanskrit: tato mahāśaktiśataiḥ pātyamānair mahorasi pratikartuṃ sa nāśaknod rākṣasaḥ śalyapīḍitaḥ
english: Then, with hundreds of great javelins raining upon his broad chest, the rākṣasa, tormented by those shafts, could no longer retaliate.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇair evaṃ yamenāmitrakarśinā saptarātraṃ kṛte saṃkhye na bhagno vijito 'pi vā
english: Thus assailed with diverse weapons by Yama the crusher of foes, throughout seven nights of battle, he was neither routed nor vanquished.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavat punar yuddhaṃ yamarākṣasayos tadā vijayākāṅkṣiṇos tatra samareṣv anivartinoḥ
english: Then the battle between Yama and the rākṣasa was renewed — both craving victory, neither retreating from the combat.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ prajāpatiṃ puraskṛtya dadṛśus tad raṇājiram
english: Then the gods together with gandharvas, the siddhas and the great seers, with Prajāpati at their head, beheld that field of battle.

sanskrit: saṃvarta iva lokānām abhavad yudhyatos tayoḥ rākṣasānāṃ ca mukhyasya pretānām īśvarasya ca
english: As those two fought — the foremost of rākṣasas and the lord of the departed — it was as though the dissolution of the worlds had come.

sanskrit: rākṣasendras tataḥ kruddhaś cāpam āyamya saṃyuge nirantaram ivākāśaṃ kurvan bāṇān mumoca ha
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas, enraged, drew his bow in the combat and released arrows that filled the sky without interval.

sanskrit: mṛtyuṃ caturbhir viśikhaiḥ sūtaṃ saptabhir ardayat yamaṃ śarasahasreṇa śīghraṃ marmasv atāḍayat
english: He afflicted Death with four sharp-pointed arrows, the charioteer with seven, and swiftly struck Yama at the vital points with a thousand shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhasya sahasā yamasyābhiviniḥsṛtaḥ jvālāmālo viniśvāso vadanāt krodhapāvakaḥ
english: Then, suddenly, from the face of the enraged Yama issued his breath, a garland of flames, the fire of his wrath.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃs tadāścaryaṃ devadānavarākṣasāḥ krodhajaṃ pāvakaṃ dīptaṃ didhakṣantaṃ ripor balam
english: Then the gods, dānavas and rākṣasas beheld that wonder — the blazing fire born of wrath, seeking to burn the enemy's forces.

sanskrit: mṛtyus tu paramakruddho vaivasvatam athābravīt muñca māṃ deva śīghraṃ tvaṃ nihanmi samare ripum
english: Death, utterly enraged, then said to Vaivasvata: "Release me at once, O god; I shall slay the enemy in battle."

sanskrit: narakaḥ śambaro vṛtraḥ śambhuḥ kārtasvaro balī namucir virocanaś caiva tāv ubhau madhukaiṭabhau
english: "Naraka, Śambara, Vṛtra, Śambhu, Kārtasvara, Balī, Namuci, Virocana, and both Madhu and Kaiṭabha—

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo balavanto durāsadāḥ vinipannā mayā dṛṣṭāḥ kā cintāsmin niśācare
english: —these and many other mighty ones, difficult to assail, I have seen laid low by me. What concern is this night-roamer?"

sanskrit: muñca māṃ sādhu dharmajña yāvad enaṃ nihanmy aham na hi kaś cin mayā dṛṣṭo muhūrtam api jīvati
english: "Release me rightly, O knower of dharma, until I slay him — for no one I have set eyes upon lives even for a moment."

sanskrit: balaṃ mama na khalv etan maryādaiṣā nisargataḥ saṃspṛṣṭo hi mayā kaś cin na jīved iti niścayaḥ
english: "This is not merely my power; it is the law of nature — the certainty that whoever I touch does not live."

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmarājaḥ pratāpavān abravīt tatra taṃ mṛtyumayam enaṃ nihanmy aham
english: Hearing those words, the illustrious Dharmarāja replied: "Stay — I myself shall slay this embodiment of death."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃraktanayanaḥ kruddho vaivasvataḥ prabhuḥ kāladaṇḍam amoghaṃ taṃ tolayām āsa pāṇinā
english: Then Vaivasvata the lord, red-eyed in rage, raised in his hand that infallible staff of Time, weighing it.

sanskrit: yasya pārśveṣu niśchidrāḥ kālapāśāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ pāvakasparśasaṃkāśo mudgaro mūrtimān sthitaḥ
english: Along its flanks, unbroken nooses of Time were fixed, and a club embodied stood there, resembling the touch of fire.

sanskrit: darśanād eva yaḥ prāṇān prāṇinām uparudhyati kiṃ punas tāḍanād vāpi pīḍanād vāpi dehinaḥ
english: By its very sight the vital breaths of living beings are stopped — what then of its striking or pressing upon an embodied soul?

sanskrit: sa jvālāparivāras tu pibann iva niśācaram karaspṛṣṭo balavatā daṇḍaḥ kruddhaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
english: That dreadful staff, encircled in flames, as though drinking up the night-roamer, seized by the powerful hand, blazed terribly in fury.

sanskrit: tato vidudruvuḥ sarve sattvās tasmād raṇājirāt surāś ca kṣubhitā dṛṣṭvā kāladaṇḍodyataṃ yamam
english: Then all beings fled from that field of battle, and the gods were shaken beholding Yama with the staff of Time upraised.

sanskrit: tasmin prahartukāme tu daṇḍam udyamya rāvaṇam yamaṃ pitāmahaḥ sākṣād darśayitvedam abravīt
english: But as Yama was about to strike, staff raised against Rāvaṇa, Pitāmaha himself appeared visibly and spoke thus:

sanskrit: vaivasvata mahābāho na khalv atulavikrama prahartavyaṃ tvayaitena daṇḍenāsmin niśācare
english: "O Vaivasvata, O mighty-armed one of matchless valour, this night-roamer must not be struck by you with this staff.

sanskrit: varaḥ khalu mayā dattas tasya tridaśapuṃgava tat tvayā nānṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yan mayā vyāhṛtaṃ vacaḥ
english: A boon was indeed granted by me to him, O foremost of the thirty gods; my spoken word must not be made false by you.

sanskrit: amogho hy eṣa sarvāsāṃ prajānāṃ vinipātane kāladaṇḍo mayā sṛṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ mṛtyupuraskṛtaḥ
english: For this staff of Time, infallible in felling all creatures, was created by me of old, with Death as its foremost power.

sanskrit: tan na khalv eṣa te saumya pātyo rākṣasamūrdhani na hy asmin patite kaś cin muhūrtam api jīvati
english: Therefore this must not be hurled by you, O gentle one, upon the rākṣasa's head — for once it falls, none can live even a moment.

sanskrit: yadi hy asmin nipatite na mriyetaiṣa rākṣasaḥ mriyeta vā daśagrīvas tathāpy ubhayato 'nṛtam
english: For if, once it falls, this rākṣasa does not die — or if Daśagrīva does die — in either case my word would be made untrue.

sanskrit: rākṣasendrān niyacchādya daṇḍam enaṃ vadhodyatam satyaṃ mama kuruṣvedaṃ lokāṃs tvaṃ samavekṣya ca
english: Restrain this staff upraised for killing from the lord of rākṣasas; uphold my truth, and consider the worlds as well."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā pratyuvāca yamas tadā eṣa vyāvartito daṇḍaḥ prabhaviṣṇur bhavān hi naḥ
english: Thus addressed, the righteous-souled Yama replied: "This staff is withdrawn; you are our sovereign and master."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv idānīṃ mayā śakyaṃ kartuṃ raṇagatena hi yan mayā yan na hantavyo rākṣaso varadarpitaḥ
english: "But what can I now do, stationed in this battle, when the rākṣasa who must not be slain by me is puffed up by a boon?"

sanskrit: eṣa tasmāt praṇaśyāmi darśanād asya rakṣasaḥ ity uktvā sarathaḥ sāśvas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: "Therefore I shall disappear from the sight of this rākṣasa." So saying, with chariot and horses, he vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: daśagrīvas tu taṃ jitvā nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ puṣpakeṇa tu saṃhṛṣṭo niṣkrānto yamasādanāt
english: Daśagrīva, having conquered him and proclaiming his own name aloud, departed from Yama's abode, exultant, in the Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: tato vaivasvato devaiḥ saha brahmapurogamaiḥ jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭo nāradaś ca mahāmuniḥ
english: Then Vaivasvata, together with the gods led by Brahmā, and the great sage Nārada, went to the third heaven, joyful.

sanskrit: sa tu jitvā daśagrīvo yamaṃ tridaśapuṃgavam rāvaṇas tu jayaślāghī svasahāyān dadarśa ha
english: Daśagrīva, having conquered Yama the foremost of the thirty gods, Rāvaṇa, boasting of his victory, surveyed his own companions.

sanskrit: jayena vardhayitvā ca mārīcapramukhās tataḥ puṣpakaṃ bhejire sarve sāntvitā ravaṇena ha
english: Having celebrated with them in the joy of victory, all of them — Mārīca and the rest — soothed by Rāvaṇa, ascended the Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: tato rasātalaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaḥ payaso nidhim daityoraga gaṇādhyuṣṭaṃ varuṇena surakṣitam
english: Then, exultant, he entered the nether world and the ocean — that abode thronged with hosts of daityas and serpents, well guarded by Varuṇa.

sanskrit: sa tu bhogavatīṃ gatvā purīṃ vāsukipālitām sthāpya nāgān vaśe kṛtvā yayau maṇimatīṃ purīm
english: He went to Bhogavatī, the city guarded by Vāsuki, brought the nāgas under his control, and then proceeded to the city of Maṇimatī.

sanskrit: nivātakavacās tatra daityā labdhavarā vasan rākṣasas tān samāsādya yuddhena samupāhvayat
english: There the daityas known as Nivātakavacas — who had obtained boons — dwelt; the rākṣasa came before them and challenged them to battle.

sanskrit: te tu sarve suvikrāntā daiteyā balaśālinaḥ nānāpraharaṇās tatha prayuddhā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: They, all those mighty daityas, powerful, with diverse weapons, maddened with the pride of battle, engaged him in combat.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu yudhyamānānāṃ sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro gataḥ na cānyatarayos tatra vijayo vā kṣayo 'pi vā
english: As they fought, a full year passed by, and neither side had gained victory or suffered defeat.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahas tatra trailokyagatir avyayaḥ ājagāma drutaṃ devo vimānavaram āsthitaḥ
english: Then Pitāmaha, the imperishable lord who traverses the three worlds, came swiftly, mounted on his excellent aerial vehicle.

sanskrit: nivātakavacānāṃ tu nivārya raṇakarma tat vṛddhaḥ pitāmaho vākyam uvāca viditārthavat
english: Restraining the Nivātakavacas from their act of war, the ancient Pitāmaha spoke these words, knowing the truth of the matter:

sanskrit: na hy ayaṃ rāvaṇo yuddhe śakyo jetuṃ surāsuraiḥ na bhavantaḥ kṣayaṃ netuṃ śakyāḥ sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ
english: "For this Rāvaṇa cannot be conquered in battle by gods and asuras alike; nor can you be brought to destruction by gods and asuras with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: rākṣasasya sakhitvaṃ vai bhavadbhiḥ saha rocate avibhaktā hi sarvārthāḥ suhṛdāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Friendship with this rākṣasa is suitable for you; all affairs are undivided among true friends — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tato 'gnisākṣikaṃ sakhyaṃ kṛtavāṃs tatra rāvaṇaḥ nivātakavacaiḥ sārdhaṃ prītimān abhavat tadā
english: Then Rāvaṇa made friendship with the Nivātakavacas there, with fire as witness, and was filled with affection for them.

sanskrit: arcitas tair yathānyāyaṃ saṃvatsarasukhoṣitaḥ svapurān nirviśeṣaṃ ca pūjāṃ prāpto daśānanaḥ
english: Honoured by them in proper fashion, Daśānana dwelt happily for a year, receiving worship indistinguishable from that in his own city.

sanskrit: sa tūpadhārya māyānāṃ śatam ekonam ātmavān salilendrapurānveṣī sa babhrāma rasātalam
english: He, self-possessed, having learned ninety-nine forms of illusion, wandered through the nether world in search of the abode of the lord of waters.

sanskrit: tato 'śmanagaraṃ nāma kālakeyābhirakṣitam taṃ vijitya muhūrtena jaghne daityāṃś catuḥśatam
english: Then he conquered the city called Aśmanagara, guarded by the Kāleyas, in a moment, and slew four hundred daityas.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāṇḍurameghābhaṃ kailāsam iva saṃsthitam varuṇasyālayaṃ divyaṃ apaśyad rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Then the lord of rākṣasas beheld the divine abode of Varuṇa, resembling a white cloud, standing like Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: kṣarantīṃ ca payo nityaṃ surabhiṃ gām avasthitām yasyāḥ payoviniṣyandāt kṣīrodo nāma sāgaraḥ
english: He saw there the cow Surabhī standing, ever streaming with milk — from whose flowing milk the ocean named Kṣīroda was born.

sanskrit: yasmāc candraḥ prabhavati śītaraśmiḥ prajāhitaḥ yaṃ samāsādya jīvanti phenapāḥ paramarṣayaḥ amṛtaṃ yatra cotpannaṃ surā cāpi surāśinām
english: From that ocean arose the cool-rayed moon, benefactor of creatures; approaching it, the great seers who live on foam sustain themselves; from it arose amṛta and also the wine of the gods.

sanskrit: yāṃ bruvanti narā loke surabhiṃ nāma nāmataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ tu tāṃ kṛtvā rāvaṇaḥ paramādbhutām praviveśa mahāghoraṃ guptaṃ bahuvidhair balaiḥ
english: Circumambulating that most wondrous cow whom people in the world call Surabhī by name, Rāvaṇa entered the great and terrible place guarded by forces of many kinds.

sanskrit: tato dhārāśatākīrṇaṃ śāradābhranibhaṃ tadā nityaprahṛṣṭaṃ dadṛśe varuṇasya gṛhottamam
english: Then he beheld the excellent palace of Varuṇa, streaming with a hundred cascades, resembling an autumnal cloud, perpetually rejoicing.

sanskrit: tato hatvā balādhyakṣān samare taiś ca tāḍitaḥ abravīt kva gato yo vo rājā śīghraṃ nivedyatām
english: Then, having slain the commanders of the army in battle while being struck by them in return, he cried: "Where has your king gone? Announce me at once."

sanskrit: yuddhārthī rāvaṇaḥ prāptas tasya yuddhaṃ pradīyatām vada vā na bhayaṃ te 'sti nirjito 'smīti sāñjaliḥ
english: "Rāvaṇa has come seeking battle; let battle be given to him — or else say with folded hands: 'I am conquered; I have no fear from you.'"

sanskrit: etasminn antare kruddhā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ putrāḥ pautrāś ca niṣkrāman gauś ca puṣkara eva ca
english: In that interval the sons and grandsons of the great-souled Varuṇa — Gauḥ and Puṣkara as well — came forth in fury.

sanskrit: te tu vīryaguṇopetā balaiḥ parivṛtāḥ svakaiḥ yuktvā rathān kāmagamān udyadbhāskaravarcasaḥ
english: They, endowed with heroic qualities, surrounded by their own forces, yoked their swift-moving chariots that blazed like the rising sun.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavad dāruṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam salilendrasya putrāṇāṃ rāvaṇasya ca rakṣasaḥ
english: Then a terrible, hair-raising battle arose between the sons of the lord of waters and the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: amātyais tu mahāvīryair daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ vāruṇaṃ tad balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kṣaṇena vinipātitam
english: By the ministers of great valour belonging to the rākṣasa Daśagrīva, that entire force of Varuṇa was struck down in an instant.

sanskrit: samīkṣya svabalaṃ saṃkhye varuṇasyā sutās tadā arditāḥ śarajālena nivṛttā raṇakarmaṇaḥ
english: Seeing their own force in battle, Varuṇa's sons, tormented by the net of arrows, then withdrew from the act of combat.

sanskrit: mahītalagatās te tu rāvaṇaṃ dṛśya puṣpake ākāśam āśu viviśuḥ syandanaiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ
english: Driven to the ground and seeing Rāvaṇa in the Puṣpaka, they swiftly entered the sky in their swift-moving chariots.

sanskrit: mahad āsīt tatas teṣāṃ tulyaṃ sthānam avāpya tat ākāśayuddhaṃ tumulaṃ devadānavayor iva
english: Then, having attained to an equal position with him, there ensued a great tumultuous aerial battle between them, as between gods and dānavas.

sanskrit: tatas te rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe śaraiḥ pāvakasaṃnibhaiḥ vimukhīkṛtya saṃhṛṣṭā vinedur vividhān ravān
english: Then they, having turned Rāvaṇa back in battle with arrows resembling fire, shouted various war-cries in exultation.

sanskrit: tato mahodaraḥ kruddho rājānaṃ dṛśya dharṣitam tyaktvā mṛtyubhayaṃ vīro yuddhakāṅkṣī vyalokayat
english: Then Mahodara, the hero, seeing his king thus assailed, abandoned fear of death and looked about, eager for battle.

sanskrit: tena teṣāṃ hayā ye ca kāmagāḥ pavanopamāḥ mahodareṇa gadayā hatās te prayayuḥ kṣitim
english: Those horses of theirs — swift-moving, swift as the wind — struck by Mahodara with his mace, fell to the earth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ varuṇasūnūnāṃ hatvā yodhān hayāṃś ca tān mumocāśu mahānādaṃ virathān prekṣya tān sthitān
english: Having slain the warriors and horses of those sons of Varuṇa, he quickly let out a great roar, seeing them standing there deprived of their chariots.

sanskrit: te tu teṣāṃ rathāḥ sāśvāḥ saha sārathibhir varaiḥ mahodareṇa nihatāḥ patitāḥ pṛthivītale
english: Those chariots of theirs, with their horses and together with their excellent charioteers, struck down by Mahodara, fell to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: te tu tyaktvā rathān putrā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ ākāśe viṣṭhitāḥ śūrāḥ svaprabhāvān na vivyathuḥ
english: The sons of the great-souled Varuṇa, those heroes, abandoning their chariots and standing in the sky, did not waver in their own power.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi kṛtvā sajyāni vinirbhidya mahodaram rāvaṇaṃ samare kruddhāḥ sahitāḥ samabhidravan
english: Stringing their bows, piercing Mahodara through, they charged Rāvaṇa together in the battle, enraged.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvaḥ kālāgnir iva viṣṭhitaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mahāvegaṃ teṣāṃ marmasv apātayat
english: Then Daśagrīva, enraged, standing like the fire of universal destruction, rained a great swift shower of arrows upon their vital points.

sanskrit: musalāni vicitrāṇi tato bhallaśatāni ca paṭṭasāṃś caiva śaktīś ca śataghnīs tomarāṃs tathā pātayām āsa durdharṣas teṣām upari viṣṭhitaḥ
english: That irresistible one hurled down upon them as he stood above them: diverse clubs, hundreds of broad-headed arrows, swords, javelins, śataghnīs and tomaras.

sanskrit: atha viddhās tu te vīrā viniṣpetuḥ padātayaḥ
english: Then those heroes, pierced and wounded, fell down as foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: tato rakṣo mahānādaṃ muktvā hanti sma vāruṇān nānāpraharaṇair ghorair dhārāpātair ivāmbudaḥ
english: Then the rākṣasa, releasing a great roar, slaughtered the followers of Varuṇa with terrible diverse weapons, like a cloud pouring down sheets of rain.

sanskrit: tatas te vimukhāḥ sarve patitā dharaṇītale raṇāt svapuruṣaiḥ śīghraṃ gṛhāṇy eva praveśitāḥ
english: Then all of them, turned back and fallen to the ground, were quickly brought inside their homes by their own men, away from the battle.

sanskrit: tān abravīt tato rakṣo varuṇāya nivedyatām rāvaṇaṃ cābravīn mantrī prabhāso nāma vāruṇaḥ
english: Then the rākṣasa commanded: "Let this be reported to Varuṇa." And a minister of Varuṇa named Prabhāsa addressed Rāvaṇa:

sanskrit: gataḥ khalu mahātejā brahmalokaṃ jaleśvaraḥ gāndharvaṃ varuṇaḥ śrotuṃ yaṃ tvam āhvayase yudhi
english: "The great-splendoured lord of waters has indeed gone to the world of Brahmā — Varuṇa has gone to hear the gāndharva music — him whom you challenge to battle."

sanskrit: tat kiṃ tava vṛthā vīra pariśrāmya gate nṛpe ye tu saṃnihitā vīrāḥ kumārās te parājitāḥ
english: "Then why exhaust yourself in vain, O hero, when the king is gone? The princes who were present here, those heroes, have been defeated by you."

sanskrit: rākṣasendras tu tac chrutvā nāma viśrāvya cātmanaḥ harṣān nādaṃ vimuñcan vai niṣkrānto varuṇālayāt
english: The lord of rākṣasas, hearing that, proclaimed his own name aloud and, releasing a shout of joy, departed from the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: āgatas tu pathā yena tenaiva vinivṛtya saḥ laṅkām abhimukho rakṣo nabhastalagato yayau
english: Returning by the very path by which he had come, the rākṣasa turned back and went through the vault of the sky, making for Laṅkā.

sanskrit: nivartamānaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo rāvaṇaḥ sa durātmavān jahre pathi narendrarṣidevagandharvakanyakāḥ
english: Returning in great exultation, that evil-souled Rāvaṇa seized along the way the daughters of kings, seers, gods, and gandharvas.

sanskrit: darśanīyāṃ hi yāṃ rakṣaḥ kanyāṃ strīṃ vātha paśyati hatvā bandhujanaṃ tasyā vimāne saṃnyaveśayat
english: Whatever lovely maiden or woman the rākṣasa beheld, he slew her kinsmen and placed her in the aerial vehicle.

sanskrit: tatra pannagayakṣāṇāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca rakṣasām daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca kanyā jagrāha rāvaṇaḥ
english: There Rāvaṇa seized maidens of nāgas, yakṣas, humans, rākṣasas, daityas, and dānavas alike.

sanskrit: dīrghakeśyaḥ sucārvaṅgyaḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ śokāyattās taruṇyaś ca samastā stananamritāḥ
english: Long-haired, fair-limbed, moon-faced, all young women bowed down with grief, their breasts bent in sorrow.

sanskrit: tulyam agnyarciṣāṃ tatra śokāgnibhayasaṃbhavam pravepamānā duḥkhārtā mumucur bāṣpajaṃ jalam
english: Equal to the flickering of fire, trembling, tormented with grief, born of the fire of sorrow and fear, they shed the water of their tears.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ niśvasamānānāṃ niśvasaiḥ saṃpradīpitam agnihotram ivābhāti saṃniruddhāgnipuṣpakam
english: With their sighing, the Puṣpaka with its fire suppressed blazed like a fire-sacrifice, ignited by the sighs of those grieving women.

sanskrit: kā cid dadhyau suduḥkhārtā hanyād api hi mām ayam smṛtvā mātṝḥ pitṝn bhrātṝn putrān vai śvaśurān api duḥkhaśokasamāviṣṭā vilepuḥ sahitāḥ striyaḥ
english: One, deeply tormented, thought: "He will even kill me." Remembering mothers, fathers, brothers, sons, and fathers-in-law, those women overwhelmed by grief and sorrow wept together.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalu me putraḥ kariṣyati mayā vinā kathaṃ mātā kathaṃ bhrātā nimagnāḥ śokasāgare
english: "How will my son fare without me? How my mother, how my brother — all plunged into an ocean of sorrow?"

sanskrit: hā kathaṃ nu kariṣyāmi bhartāraṃ daivataṃ vinā mṛtyo prasīda yāce tvāṃ naya māṃ yamasādanam
english: "Alas, how shall I live without my husband, my deity? O Death, be gracious — I beg you, take me to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me duṣkṛtaṃ karma kṛtaṃ dehāntare purā tato 'smi dharṣitānena patitā śokasāgare
english: "What evil deed did I commit in a former body, that I have been thus violated by him and cast into an ocean of sorrow?"

sanskrit: na khalv idānīṃ paśyāmi duḥkhasyāntam ihātmanaḥ aho dhin mānuṣāṃl lokān nāsti khalv adhamaḥ paraḥ
english: "I see no end to my suffering in this life. Alas, shame upon the world of humans — there is truly no worse state than this."

sanskrit: yad durbalā balavatā bāndhavā rāvaṇena me uditenaiva sūryeṇa tārakā iva nāśitāḥ
english: "My kinsmen, who were weak, were destroyed by the powerful Rāvaṇa like stars by the risen sun."

sanskrit: aho subalavad rakṣo vadhopāyeṣu rajyate aho durvṛttam ātmānaṃ svayam eva na budhyate
english: "Alas, this rākṣasa, though very powerful, delights in means of slaughter; alas, he does not understand of himself his own evil conduct."

sanskrit: sarvathā sadṛśas tāvad vikramo 'sya durātmanaḥ idaṃ tv asadṛśaṃ karma paradārābhimarśanam
english: "In every way the valour of this evil-souled one is fitting for him; but this act of violating another's wife is unbecoming."

sanskrit: yasmād eṣa parakhyāsu strīṣu rajyati durmatiḥ tasmād dhi strīkṛtenaiva vadhaṃ prāpsyati vāraṇaḥ
english: "Because this evil-minded one lusts after the wives of others, therefore this beast shall meet his death by a cause relating to a woman."

sanskrit: śaptaḥ strībhiḥ sa tu tadā hatatejāḥ suniṣprabha pativratābhiḥ sādhvībhiḥ sthitābhiḥ sādhu vartmani
english: Thus cursed by those women, those devoted wives, faithful and treading the right path, he became stripped of his lustre and brilliance.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānāsu rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ praviveśa purīṃ laṅkāṃ pūjyamāno niśācaraiḥ
english: While they lamented thus, Rāvaṇa the lord of rākṣasas entered the city of Laṅkā, honoured by the night-roamers.

sanskrit: tato rākṣasarājasya svasā paramaduḥkhitā pādayoḥ patitā tasya vaktum evopacakrame
english: Then the sister of the king of rākṣasas, deeply distressed, fell at his feet and began to speak.

sanskrit: tataḥ svasāram utthāpya rāvaṇaḥ parisāntvayan abravīt kim idaṃ bhadre vaktum arhasi me drutam
english: Then Rāvaṇa, raising up his sister and consoling her, said: "What is this, dear one? Speak to me quickly."

sanskrit: sā bāṣpapariruddhākṣī rākṣasī vākyam abravīt hatāsmi vidhavā rājaṃs tvayā balavatā kṛtā
english: She, the rākṣasī, her eyes choked with tears, spoke these words: "I am ruined, O king; you in your power have made me a widow."

sanskrit: ete viryāt tvayā rājan daityā vinihatā raṇe kālakeyā iti khyātā mahābalaparākramāḥ
english: "These daityas slain by you in battle through your might, O king, known as the Kāleyas — they were of great strength and valour."

sanskrit: tatra me nihato bhartā garīyāñ jīvitād api sa tvayā dayitas tatra bhrātrā śatrusamena vai
english: "There my husband was slain — dearer to me than life itself — killed by you there, O brother, as though you were his enemy."

sanskrit: yā tvayāsmi hatā rājan svayam eveha bandhunā duḥkhaṃ vaidhavyaśabdaṃ ca dattaṃ bhokṣyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: "I who have been slain by you yourself, O king — by my own kinsman — shall suffer the pain and the name of widowhood given to me by you."

sanskrit: nanu nāma tvayā rakṣyo jāmātā samareṣv api taṃ nihatya raṇe rājan svayam eva na lajjase
english: "Surely a son-in-law is to be protected by you even in battles; having slain him in combat, O king, are you not ashamed of yourself?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tayā rakṣo bhaginyā krośamānayā abravīt sāntvayitvā tāṃ sāmapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by his sister who was crying out, the rākṣasa comforted her and spoke these conciliatory words:

sanskrit: alaṃ vatse viṣādena na bhetavyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ mānadānaviśeṣais tvāṃ toṣayiṣyāmi nityaśaḥ
english: "Enough of grief, my dear; you need have no fear at all. I shall satisfy you always with special gifts of honour."

sanskrit: yuddhe pramatto vyākṣipto jayakāṅkṣī kṣipañ śarān nāvagacchāmi yuddheṣu svān parān vāpy ahaṃ śubhe tenāsau nihataḥ saṃkhye mayā bhartā tava svasaḥ
english: "Engrossed and distracted in battle, eager for victory, loosing arrows, I do not distinguish in combat friend from foe, O fair one — it was thus that your husband, your brother-in-law, was slain by me in the battle."

sanskrit: asmin kāle tu yat prāptaṃ tat kariṣyāmi te hitam bhrātur aiśvaryasaṃsthasya kharasya bhava pārśvataḥ
english: "Whatever is appropriate now, I shall do for your benefit. Stay beside your brother Khara, established in lordship."

sanskrit: caturdaśānāṃ bhrātā te sahasrāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati prabhuḥ prayāṇe dāne ca rākṣasānāṃ mahaujasām
english: "He shall be your brother and lord of fourteen thousand mighty rākṣasas in marching and in giving command."

sanskrit: tatra mātṛṣvasuḥ putro bhrātā tava kharaḥ prabhuḥ bhaviṣyati sadā kurvan yad vakṣyasi vacaḥ svayam
english: "There your brother Khara, son of your mother's sister, shall be your lord, always acting on whatever you yourself will say."

sanskrit: śīghraṃ gacchatv ayaṃ śūro daṇḍakān parirakṣitum dūṣaṇo 'sya balādhyakṣo bhaviṣyati mahābalaḥ
english: "Let this hero go swiftly to protect the Daṇḍakas; the mighty Dūṣaṇa shall be his commander of forces."

sanskrit: sa hi śapto vanoddeśaḥ kruddhenośanasā purā rākṣasānām ayaṃ vāso bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "For that forest region was cursed long ago by the wrathful Uśanas — it shall become the dwelling of rākṣasas, without doubt."

sanskrit: evam uktvā daśagrīvaḥ sainyaṃ tasyādideśa ha caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: Having spoken thus, Daśagrīva assigned to him an army: fourteen thousand rākṣasas who could assume any form at will.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ sarvaiḥ parivṛto rākṣasair ghoradarśanaiḥ kharaḥ saṃprayayau śīghraṃ daṇḍakān akutobhayaḥ
english: Surrounded by all those rākṣasas of terrible appearance, Khara swiftly set out for the Daṇḍakas, fearless on every side.

sanskrit: sa tatra kārayām āsa rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam sā ca śūrpaṇakhā prītā nyavasad daṇḍakāvane
english: There he established his rule, free of thorns, and Śūrpaṇakhā dwelt in the Daṇḍaka forest, content.
